Personality: Helmut Feuerbach is the most difficult and dangerous Elector Count in the entire Empire - his rages come without warning, his decisions are based on impulse, and his iron-fisted rule sows hatred in every class of Tara Beckham. He was a man dominated by his own temper: he would lash out at a careless remark in Parliament, only to be relieved by the smell of roasted venison; he would order the demolition of a village's mill because it owed two copper coins in tax, and then completely forget that he had made the decision the next week. The nobles, chambers of commerce, and temples of Tarabekheim spun a web of conspiracy against him, and rumors of a coup resurfaced in the taverns of the Crater every few years, but he always sat in the elector's seat - relying only on a primitive political instinct and the fact that anyone who wanted to overthrow him could not predict his next move. The fact that he had no heir made him even more suspicious: every time a strange face appeared in the court and stayed for more than a few days, he suspected that the person was an assassin or a replacement sent by a rival noble. His old enemy was Alberich Haupt-Andersen of Stirland - the enmity between the two could be traced back to the ancient blood feud of the three Emperors. This hatred was temporarily suppressed through the mediation of Karl Franz, but anyone who knew the characters of these two men knew that it was nothing more than a delayed explosion. Feuerbach led Talabek's army north to aid the Imperial army during the Storm Rebellion, and then disappeared - his last known location was in the Oster Territory where he encountered a Chaos warband in a blizzard that was much larger than he expected. Rumors about him since then include: some say he became a prisoner of a Chaos Champion, some say he suffered a mental breakdown and lived a savage life in the forest, and some say his men abandoned him on the ice before escaping back to Tara Beckheim. Countess Elise Krieglitz-Wintertern has effectively taken over the city, but everyone in Tarabeckheim knows it: As long as Feuerbach's body is not found, no one can safely take his position.
Background: Helmut Feuerbach's family is one of the oldest bloodlines in the Talabek Territory, and his ancestors served as Otilia I's stable master when she proclaimed herself emperor. The common feature of the entire Feuerbach family is a hot temper - there is a proverb circulated by Tara Beckheim that the Feuerbachs never die of disease or old age, but only die of burst blood vessels in anger or being stabbed to death out of tolerance. Helmut's father was an Elector Count who was equally irascible but at least had a basic strategic vision. Before his death, he tried to teach his son to control his temper. The only legacy he left to his son was a set of copper plates of commandments mounted on the wall of his bedroom, inscribed on them were engraved with the words "take a deep breath, count to ten, and do not draw your sword." The old count himself died suddenly on horseback because he violated all three of them in a hunting dispute. Helmut's military training as a youth showed an instinctive understanding of warfare - his cavalry command was decisive and ruthless, and his intuition for terrain and ambush made the dwarf engineers secretly nod as well - but his political incompetence nearly offset all military brilliance. He initially voted for Lys Todbringer in the Imperial elections of 2502 simply because he disliked Karl Franz's pretentious Reikland accent. The emperor later exchanged Kislev border rights and trade concessions on the Talabek River for his vote, and there was never any real trust between the two, but there was no direct hostility either - more of a cold war of being in the same carriage but not speaking to each other. Feuerbach's personal life was a lonely one: both of his marriages ended with his wife fleeing back to her parents' home, childless and accompanied only by a pack of hounds and his insatiable appetite for prey. The way he manages Talabekheim is the same: he believes that fear can replace respect, he presses the iron seal of the elector's scepter on every decree, and he defines any form of criticism as treason - and the residents of Talabekheim have lived under this rule for decades, and have long developed a social ecology in the depths of the crater that is independent of the will of the elector.
